slot.brief: Three alcohols (1°, 2°, 3° including a cyclic one) subjected to Lucas test; predict turbidity order with time and explain via carbocation stability.

stem: At room temperature, three alcohols are treated with Lucas reagent. Which order gives turbidity from earliest to latest, with no turbidity last?

verdicts.working: Lucas test rate: tertiary > secondary > primary. Thus 2-methylpropan-2-ol reacts first, cyclohexanol next, and butan-1-ol shows no turbidity at room temperature.

working:
Lucas test proceeds mainly by $\text{S}_\text{N}1$; rate follows carbocation stability.
$3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ$
2-methylpropan-2-ol: immediate turbidity; cyclohexanol: turbidity after a few minutes; butan-1-ol: no turbidity at room temperature.

Independent check: Lucas test rate: tertiary > secondary > primary. Thus 2-methylpropan-2-ol reacts first, cyclohexanol next, and butan-1-ol shows no turbidity at room temperature.
solution: Lucas test proceeds mainly by the $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism; the rate follows carbocation stability, $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ$. Thus 2-methylpropan-2-ol gives immediate turbidity, cyclohexanol reacts after a few minutes, and butan-1-ol gives no turbidity at room temperature.
